title: Clear the nullable warnings
summary: Instead of silencing CS8603 with !, let Product?, NotNullWhen and MemberNotNullWhen carry it.

turns.user: turned nullable on and got 600 warnings. just slap ! on all of them for now

assistant.body: The ! only silences the check, the NullReferenceException at runtime stays. Start with Find returning Product?, so the missing case is visible in the type.

turns.user: there are like 200 call sites. am I writing an if in every one of them? throwing is fine when it's missing

assistant.body: Then split the call sites. Where the product must exist, Get throws for you; where you want to check, TryGet does it. NotNullWhen on the out parameter means the true branch is warning free. It needs a using for System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.

turns.user: DescribeCategory still trips CS8602. Category can be null too, forgot to mention

assistant.body: That was my bad assumption. Make Category nullable and move the check into a property annotated with MemberNotNullWhen. Past the if the compiler treats Category as non null, so no ! anywhere.

turns.user: build is still red. CS8618 on _bySku. and the exception message, sku on its own tells me nothing about which key

assistant.body: The uninitialized field and the message are one line each, so sed covers both. I am keeping the comparer case sensitive, which is the default.

turns.user: changed my mind, DescribeCategory should return an empty string. the view will render UNCATEGORIZED

assistant.body: Only the fallback changes. The return type stays string, so no call site is affected.
